newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee volatile vs forward dlr, premia end up.
newsitem.headline: India rupee volatile vs forward dlr, premia end up.

text.p: * Spot rupee ends at 35.87/88 against the dollar on Wednesday compared with 35.88/89 opening.
* The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) buys forward dollars from select banks in swap deals but roll-over of earlier deals by a leading financial institution helps push up forward premia.
* Six-month annualised forward premia ends at 7.08 percent, up from the previous close of 6.69 percent.
* RBI's forward dollar purchases overshadow its purchases from spot market - the central bank buys dollars at 35.88, its highest purchase in recent months, dealers say.
Active buying of forward dollars in the swap market by the RBI dominated the action on Wednesday, dealers said.
Spot August dollars opened at 1.32/1.35 rupees.
The RBI picked up spot August dollars in the morning swap deals at 1.31/1.32 rupees.
Roll-over of large positions by an Indian financial institution reversed the sentiment, pushing up premia in later trade. RBI came a second time, buying spot August upto 1.35 rupees, dealers said.
August dollar premium closed at 1.40 rupees.
Spotlight on the forward dollar disguised RBI's buying in the spot market, dealers said.

"They were ready to buy any amount from anyone," said a dealer. He said RBI bought dollars at 35.88 rupees -- its highest purchase price in recent months. RBI's purchases from spot market could easily exceed $50 million, one dealer said.
"Their objective is to keep dollar from going down and to shore up their reserves," said a dealer about RBI's motives.

Thanks to aggressive dollar buying from the spot and swap markets in recent months, the redemption of India Development Bonds later this week would pass of peacefully without upsetting the rupee, dealers said.
